title: OpenStage object
description: The envelope every object carries. `type` decides what is valid in `content`. See docs/format-spec.md.

altSuggestion.description: Optional, editor and Capture only. A description the computer worked out (for example from the name of what was clicked in a recording) that the author has not approved. The course never uses it: the object still has no alt text, and the checker still asks for it, until the author uses the suggestion (it becomes altText and this is removed) or writes their own.

basis.description: What the suggestion was worked out from, in words the author can read.

states.description: The looks the object can take besides its own. A name is 1 to 40 characters with no space at either end. hover, visited and disabled are used by the course on their own; any other name is used only when a rule applies it. The name normal is the object's own appearance and cannot be a look (the validator says so in plain words).

group.description: Editor only. Objects on one layer with the same group id are grouped: the editor selects, moves, copies and deletes them together. Absent means not in a group. The published course ignores it.

locked.description: Editor only. True means the editor refuses to move, resize, rotate or delete the object until it is unlocked. Absent means unlocked. The published course ignores it.

allOf.$comment: Non-decorative objects need real alt text.
Decorative objects must not carry alt text.
Interactive objects must be reachable by keyboard: tabOrder 1 or more.
A hotspot is a transparent button with a name, and nothing else: it has no content of its own.
A video may carry an audio description: cues, each with a time and the words that say what the picture shows.
Video needs a caption track or a narration script.
Audio needs a caption track, a narration script or a transcript. A transcript is what an audio-only clip needs.

timing.$comment: When the object appears and disappears, counted from when its layer is shown (the slide opening, for the base layer), or from a moment in a video or audio clip. Milliseconds, like a slide's duration.

appear.description: time: start milliseconds after the layer is shown. narration: start milliseconds after this object's own narration starts. media: start milliseconds into the video or audio clip named by media. click: start milliseconds after the learner presses Show next item for step number step.

step.description: Only with appear click, and then required: which press of Show next item shows this object. Objects with the same step show together.

media.description: Only with appear media: the id of a video or audio object on the same slide, whose playing time this object follows.

until.description: Optional, added in 0.38.0. The object goes away when the learner shows step `step` (the steps of Show next item; on a slide with autoSteps, when that step comes by itself), `start` milliseconds after it. It is how an exit effect that waits for a click in PowerPoint comes across. A step that only has objects going away is still a step to press. If `visibleFor` is also given, the object goes at whichever comes first.

visibleFor.description: How long it stays once shown, or null to stay until the layer is hidden or the slide ends. With appear media it is a length of the video or audio clip, not of the clock.

paragraphs.description: Optional, added in 0.41.0, and only for a text object. A timing for each paragraph (a heading, a paragraph, a quotation, or a list item with the lists inside it, counted in the order they come in the text), so the text can come in or go away one paragraph at a time. Each is a timing of its own (when it appears: at a time or at a step; when it goes away), counted from when the layer is shown, and the object's own timing, animation and narration apply to the whole box as they always did. A paragraph that is not given a timing is always there. Each paragraph that waits for a step is one of the steps of Show next item.

partTiming.$comment: The timing of one paragraph of a text (see timing.paragraphs): the same as an object's, except that it cannot follow a clip or a narration, and has no paragraphs of its own.

appear.description: time: start milliseconds after the layer is shown. click: start milliseconds after the learner presses Show next item for step number step.

step.description: Only with appear click, and then required.

until.description: The paragraph goes away when the learner shows step `step`, `start` milliseconds after it.

animation.$comment: How an object arrives and leaves when its timing shows and hides it. An entrance plays when the object appears (including when the slide opens, for an object that is there from the start). An exit plays when it disappears at the end of its time.

effect.description: none: no effect. fade: opacity only. slideLeft, slideRight, slideTop, slideBottom: arrives from that side, or leaves toward it. wipeLeft, wipeRight, wipeTop, wipeBottom (added in 0.40.0): shown across from that edge, or hidden back toward it, with nothing moving. zoom: grows from slightly smaller, or shrinks to it.

duration.description: Milliseconds. Short on purpose: a longer movement is a distraction and a barrier.

contentDownload.$comment: A file the learner can save to their own device. The description says what the file is, so learners know before they download it, and the author confirms the file is accessible.

contentTimer.$comment: A countdown. It starts when the layer it is on is shown. The rules on the timer that answer timerEnd run when the time is up. The learner can always turn it off, and can add time when extendBy is more than 0.

label.description: The words above the clock, such as Time left.

extendBy.description: How many seconds the Add time button gives, or 0 for no such button.

contentResults.$comment: The learner's score, whether they passed, and optionally each question. Filled in by the player from the quiz.

contentCertificate.$comment: A certificate for a learner who passed. The learner types their own name, then prints it or saves it as a PDF.

enlargeable.$comment: Optional, added in 0.43.0. True gives the picture an Enlarge button that opens it as big as the window allows. Absent means false. Not for a decorative picture.

icon.description: Optional. A small picture drawn beside the label. It is decoration: the label is the button's name.

iconPlacement.description: Which side of the label the icon is on. Before when absent.

iconShape.$comment: One drawn part of an icon. Only these tags and these attributes exist, so an icon can never carry a script or a link.

contentIcon.$comment: An icon drawn in a 24 by 24 box with a rounded outline in the object's colour. The shapes are kept in the project, so the course does not depend on the icon set.

set.description: The icon set it came from. Lucide is ISC licensed, and a course that uses it names it on its credits page.

min.$comment: For kinds slider and dial (added in 0.42.0): the lowest value. The variable is a number.

max.$comment: For kinds slider and dial: the highest value.

step.$comment: For kinds slider and dial: the distance between values. More than 0, with no more than 3 decimals.

unit.$comment: For kinds slider and dial: a word or sign after the number, such as % or days.

startLabel.$comment: For kinds slider and dial: what the lowest end means.

endLabel.$comment: For kinds slider and dial: what the highest end means.

showValue.$comment: For kinds slider and dial: whether the number is shown beside the control. Absent means it is.

characters.$comment: For kind character: which people from the project's cast the learner can choose between. The variable then holds the id of the one chosen.

scenarioLine.$comment: One thing said or told in a scenario: by the narrator (speaker null), by the learner's own character (speaker "you"), or by a person from the project's cast (their id). Plain text.

pose.$comment: Optional. The id of one of the speaker's poses, to show them in it instead of their picture. Absent or null means their picture.

narration.$comment: What the learner hears when this line is shown. Same shape as an object's narration. Null means the line can only be read.

next.description: The situation this choice leads to. A situation with no choices is an ending.

add.description: Added to a number variable when this choice is made. A negative number takes away.

response.description: What happens straight after this choice, shown before the next situation.

prompt.description: The question put to the learner above the choices. Empty means the title names the choices.

contentScenario.$comment: A branching scenario: situations the learner responds to by choosing, each choice leading to another situation, until an ending (a situation with no choices).

you.$comment: The name of a string variable that holds the id of the person the learner chose to be (see the input kind character). Null means the learner is just "you".

allowRetry.description: Whether the learner can take back their last choice and choose again.

finishedVariable.$comment: A true/false variable set to true when the learner reaches an ending, so rules can carry on from there.

reflection.description: Something for the learner to think about, shown with the review of their path at an ending.

time.description: Milliseconds into the video when the description starts.

text.description: What the picture shows, in words a learner can read. An empty one is reported by the validator.

pause.description: Whether the video waits while the description is spoken (an extended description).

narration.$comment: What the learner hears at that time. Same shape as an object's narration. Null means the description can only be read.

guided.$comment: For kind labeledGraphic (added in 0.45.0): also step through the markers in order with Previous and Next buttons. Absent means false.

graphic.$comment: For kind labeledGraphic (added in 0.44.0): the picture the markers sit on. alt says what the whole picture shows and is checked by the validator.

x.$comment: For kind labeledGraphic: where this item's marker sits, as a percentage of the picture's width, to the middle of the marker.

y.$comment: For kind labeledGraphic: where this item's marker sits, as a percentage of the picture's height.

narration.$comment: What the learner hears when this item is opened. Same shape as an object's narration.

shuffle.description: Only for multipleChoice and multipleResponse. Show the answers in a different order to each learner, the same order each time that learner comes back. Absent means the author's order.

minWords.description: Only for essay. The fewest words that count as an answer. 0 means any answer at all. An essay is not marked: it earns its points once it has this many words.

passage.description: Only for whichWord. The passage the learner reads, with each right word in [square brackets].

keys.description: Only for shortcut. Every keyboard shortcut that is right, each written like Ctrl+Shift+S.

announce.description: What a screen reader says when a rule applies this look. Not said when the course applies the look on its own (pointer over it, keyboard focus, used).

action.description: nextSlide, previousSlide and replaySlide act on the course itself, so their target is empty.

operation.description: Only for setVariable. set (the default) puts value in the variable; add adds value (1 if there is none) to a number variable.

importProvenance.description: An object made from a shape in a PowerPoint deck. `base` is the object as the import made it, so a changed deck can be compared with what the author has done since (a three-way comparison).

slideId.description: The deck's own number for the slide the shape was on (p:sldId), which stays the same when slides are moved.

sourceHash.description: A fingerprint of the shape as the deck had it, so an unchanged shape is known without comparing it.

slideImportProvenance.description: A slide made from a slide in a PowerPoint deck.

shapes.description: The shapes of the slide that the import brought in, by their number on the slide, so one the author deleted is not brought back.

animation.description: Optional, added in 0.39.0. What the import gave the timing and animation of each shape that has an effect in the deck, by the shape's number on the slide, so a changed deck's animation can be compared with what the author has done since.

notes.description: Optional, added in 0.39.0. Set when the slide's speaker notes were made the narration of one of its objects: that shape's number on the slide, and the words the notes gave, so a changed deck's notes can be compared with what the author has done since.

base.description: Optional, on a slide. What the Capture module made for this step, so that when the steps change the slide can be brought up to date without losing what the author changed: the slide's name, the picture it was made with, and for each thing it made (by its part, such as 'words' or 'layer-hint/message') the object's id, its layer, and a fingerprint of each part of the object as made.

fields.description: A fingerprint of each part of the object as made (its name, geometry, content, style, accessibility, states, triggers, timing, animation and narration), so a change the author made to one part does not stop another part being brought up to date.
